title: Pricing by hours per project for Mobile massage
audience: Mobile massage therapists who quote a session visit from the hours it takes, including set-up, clean-down and travel, and who need a price that covers cost and earns a margin.
learningOutcomes: Calculate a cost per productive hour from your own costs and chargeable time
Estimate a home session in hours, including set-up, clean-down and travel
Build a quote from hours, a rate and a margin, and state its basis and exclusions

instruction.heading: Why hours are the starting unit
instruction.body: A mobile session is mostly time: the drive to the client, the set-up in a room you do not control, the session itself, the clean-down and the write-up. Hours turn each of these into a cost. A flat price with no hours behind it hides the travel that eats into a short day, and it cannot be defended when a client asks why a home visit costs what it does.

instruction.heading: Build the cost per productive hour
instruction.body: Take the total cost of running the business over a period and divide it by the chargeable hours in that period. Costs include vehicle running costs, insurance, registration, the table and its covers, linen or its laundering, oils and products, disposable items, booking software, phone and administration. If you pay yourself a wage, include it as a cost line so the figure covers your own time. If you employ staff, on-costs apply, but the award position for massage therapists was not confirmed by the sources read, so check the award coverage for your role before using any award figure. Check the ATO’s current vehicle rate yourself before you claim vehicle costs; this lesson does not state one. Use chargeable hours, not paid hours. Illustrative figure only: $65 AUD an hour.

instruction.heading: Estimate the hours
instruction.body: Break each visit into tasks: the session, set-up and clean-down, travel to the client and the write-up. Estimate each task at a standard speed and record it as a named line. Add an allowance for delays outside your control, such as a late client or a parking problem. Xero Australia gives a range of 10 to 20 per cent added to job estimates for unexpected work (3 September 2026). That is a general range, not a massage benchmark, so size your allowance from your own records. After each visit, record the actual minutes and the reason for any difference.

instruction.heading: Turn hours into a price
instruction.body: Multiply the hours by the cost per productive hour to get the cost of the visit. Divide that cost by one minus your target margin to get the price, which gives a margin on price rather than a mark-up on cost. Add a margin that reflects your target and the risk, such as a home with poor access or a tight schedule. Apply your minimum charge. Once you are registered for GST, include GST in the price. The ATO gives a $75,000 GST turnover threshold for registration (ATO, Registering for GST, updated 14 September 2026).

instruction.heading: Keep the quote honest
instruction.body: A quote should state the session, the hours or price basis, the travel line, the exclusions, what the client must provide, and how long the quote is valid. Do not show your internal cost per hour unless your policy says to. Record every change to the session, such as a longer treatment or an added step, and re-quote before the work starts. A quote with no exclusions invites disputes.

instruction.heading: Review your estimates
instruction.body: Compare estimated and actual minutes for at least the first ten visits of each type. Carters Trade Leader, a New Zealand publisher, makes a general point: use the gap between quoted and actual labour to correct the next quote (1 October 2025). If the variance is regularly above your threshold, change the standard time, the margin or the scope rules.

procedure: Gather the year’s total business costs and the chargeable hours achieved in the same period.
Divide total costs by chargeable hours to get the cost per productive hour, and include your own wage as a line if you pay one.
Break each visit into tasks and estimate each task time as a range.
Add set-up, clean-down and travel as named lines.
Multiply total hours by the cost per productive hour, then apply the margin for risk and target.
Apply the materials policy and the minimum charge.
Write the quote with scope, hours basis, travel line, exclusions, client inputs and validity.
Record actual minutes after each visit and compare them with the estimate.

workedExamples.situation: Illustrative figures only, not market rates. A mobile massage therapist visits one client for a 60-minute session. Set-up and clean-down take 10 minutes, and the drive to the client takes 20 minutes. The cost per productive hour is $65 AUD (illustrative). The target margin on price is 25 per cent (illustrative).
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the cost of the visit, what is the price with a 25 per cent margin on price, and how does the price compare with the marketplace range in the sources?
workedExamples.reasoning: The visit is 90 minutes, which is 1.5 hours, so the cost is 1.5 multiplied by $65 AUD, which is $97.50 AUD. A 25 per cent margin on price means the price is the cost divided by 0.75, which gives $130.00 AUD. Oneflare gives a marketplace range of $55 to $100 per session, undated and not a benchmark, and it says home visits may incur a travel fee. The $130.00 AUD price sits above that range, and the difference is the travel and set-up time the range may not include. The therapist shows those lines on the quote so the client can see what the price covers.

equipmentAndPpe: Time log for each visit, with estimated and actual columns
A timer or phone clock for set-up, session and clean-down minutes

commonErrors.error: Pricing from the hourly wage alone
commonErrors.prevention: Include on-costs, vehicle, equipment, consumables, insurance and administration in the cost per productive hour.

commonErrors.error: Counting paid hours as productive hours
commonErrors.prevention: Use chargeable hours only when calculating the cost per productive hour.

commonErrors.error: Leaving out travel, set-up and clean-down time
commonErrors.prevention: Add these as named lines on every quote.
List what is excluded, what the client provides, and the access assumptions, such as a firm, level surface.

commonErrors.error: Never comparing estimates with actual minutes
commonErrors.prevention: Record actual minutes after each visit and review the variance monthly.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: This is pricing guidance only. Misleading statements about prices are prohibited (ACCC, Setting prices: what’s allowed, 15 July 2026). The ACCC’s 2015 drip-pricing case was about online fees, so applying it to a mobile travel fee is an inference. State or territory fair-trading rules also apply and differ between states and territories.

Award coverage for massage therapists is not confirmed. The Hair and Beauty Industry Award 2020 (MA000005) was checked for hairdressing and beauty, and massage was not seen in the clauses checked. Do not apply the award rates in other courses to a massage therapist without checking the award coverage for your role.

qualityStandard: Each quote shows scope, hours or price basis, travel line, exclusions, client inputs and validity.
The cost per productive hour is calculated from your own records and dated.
Actual minutes are recorded for at least the first ten visits of each type and compared with the estimate.
No quote is issued without a margin decision and a minimum-charge check.
documentationEvidence: Cost per productive hour worksheet, dated, with the source of each figure
Quote showing scope, hours basis, travel line, exclusions and validity
Visit time log with estimated and actual minutes
summary: Hours make a mobile session visible, so start every quote from hours.
Cost per productive hour uses chargeable time, not paid time.
Travel, set-up and clean-down are named lines, not hidden extras.
Compare estimates with actual minutes, and change the method when they diverge.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which costs belong in the cost per productive hour?
options: Only the hourly wage of the lowest-paid worker and nothing else from the accounts or the rent
The price the client pays, plus the deposit, the late fee and the crew bonus paid
The average hourly rate of competitors in the local area and their fees for the whole year
Wages with on-costs, vehicle, equipment, consumables, insurance and administration, divided by chargeable hours

knowledgeChecks.question: A session estimated at 60 minutes takes 85. What is the right response?
options: Record the actual minutes, find the cause, and adjust the estimate and future quotes
Leave the estimate, since the client has already paid and the session is finished
Reduce paid hours for the therapist on the next visit and skip the morning break
Raise the price for this client's next visit only and no one else is charged more

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does a quote need an exclusions list?
options: To hide the margin from the client and to keep the rates a secret from the crew
To make the quote longer and to fill up the page with more text and words for the client
To show what the price covers, so scope changes can be priced and disputes are reduced
To lower the client's expectations and to make the job seem much smaller than it is
